question: Refer to the exhibit. The communication between the web server and the application server experiences poor performance. The network engineer must collect the traffic between the two servers, including the payload, for more investigation. The collected data must be sent from the remote site to the headquarters. Which action accomplishes this goal?
context: Topology: Remote Site has Web Server and Application Server connected to N5K-1, which connects via L3 MPLS to N5K-2 at HQ, which connects to a Monitor Server.
imageNote: Diagram: Remote Site (Web Server and Application Server connected to N5K-1) links via an L3 MPLS cloud to HQ (N5K-2 connected to a Monitor Server).
options: Configure NetFlow on N5K-1 to send the data to the monitor server.
Configure SNMP on N5K-1 to send the data to the monitor server.
Configure a SPAN session between N5K-1 and N5K-2.
Configure an ERSPAN session between N5K-1 and N5K-2.
theory: SPAN only mirrors traffic locally within a single switch or across switches on a shared Layer 2 segment; carrying a full copy of traffic, including payload, across a routed multi-hop path such as an MPLS L3 WAN between sites requires ERSPAN, which encapsulates the mirrored frames in a GRE/IP tunnel that can be routed like any other IP traffic to a distant destination address. NetFlow only exports flow summary statistics rather than full payload, and SNMP reports counters/state, neither of which meets the requirement to collect the actual traffic including payload, and plain SPAN cannot span a routed WAN link at all. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — ERSPAN vs. SPAN for Remote Traffic Capture)
